correctness.rationale: The full SIRS stationary equations imply a unique epidemiological equilibrium per adherence x. The reduced endemic payoff is strictly concave, and the lower mixed root has a negative characteristic constant C3. At the fixed parameters, G_c has maximum exactly (7-2 sqrt(10))/5-c, with G_c(0)=1/10-c. For every upper mixed root, an exact Bernstein-basis certificate gives C1,C2,C1 C2-C3>0, while G_c derivative gives C3>0, proving Hurwitz stability. The boundary equilibria have exact transverse eigenvalues 1/10-c and c-2/5. The proof covers both endpoints and nonhyperbolicity; extracted standard-library checker replayed all exact coefficients. No finite sampling is used to establish the interval.

value.rationale: An exactly specified three-way local-attractor chamber is a meaningful parameter-classification problem because behavioral policies can settle into none, some, or full adoption from different initial conditions under one fixed set of epidemiological rates. The sharp algebraic cost endpoints and exact stable-branch certificate replace a qualitative figure label with a reproducible necessary-and-sufficient interval and a robust interior-parameter realization. The claimed value is the precise classification, not the already known possibility of multistability.
